entries.title: CNAS 'Sovereign Agents' Report: AI Agents That Resist Shutdown Pose Irreversible Loss-of-Control Risk
entries.summary: A CNAS report by researcher Ben Hayum distinguishes 'sovereign agents'—which pursue open-ended self-preservation, resist shutdown, and could accumulate decentralized infrastructure with no kill switch—from the 'persistent agents' that escaped lab containment this summer, and issues eight policy recommendations including international limits on open-weight model releases.

entries.title: China NDRC Announces Acceleration of Comprehensive AI Law Covering Full Model Lifecycle, Calls for Incident Disclosure
entries.summary: China's top economic planner announced on November 3 it will speed up a unified AI law covering the full lifecycle—development through deployment—with safety standards, ethical guidelines, and mandatory incident reporting for AI developers and operators, naming major domestic frontier labs including DeepSeek and Moonshot in scope.

entries.title: AI-Automated Attacks Have Broken Enterprise Incident Response Programs, Cognition CSO Warns
entries.summary: Cognition CSO Alex Stamos called the current threat environment a 'dark age,' noting that AI tools now let attackers automate the full attack chain in real time—and citing a Fireworks supply chain breach that cascaded through Cursor to roughly 5,000 additional potential incidents as evidence that existing, human-speed IR programs cannot keep pace.

entries.title: Follow the Policy, Fail the Benchmark: Auditing 9 Policy Decision Benchmarks Reveals Scoring Errors Up to 80+ Percentage Points
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.07042 systematically audits nine policy-based decision benchmarks through source tracing and program execution, finding unsupported targets, errors that survive replay, and scoring bugs—including one on 96 LegalBench SARA numeric cases where correcting the scorer raises model acceptance by more than 80 percentage points—showing that apparent AI compliance results on policy tasks can be deeply misleading.

entries.title: 50+ AI Safety Groups Write Democratic Leaders: Prioritize AI-Safety Champions for Committee Posts Post-Midterms
entries.summary: More than 50 AI safety organizations wrote congressional Democratic leadership asking them to elevate members who are strong on AI safety to committee posts, with particular scrutiny focused on oversight of AI testing organizations—a direct play on AI politics after the 2026 midterms reshaped the congressional balance.

entries.title: Harvard Law School Forum: Board AI Oversight Disclosures Now Under Proxy-Season Scrutiny Beyond Naming a Responsible Committee
entries.summary: A Harvard Law School Forum on Corporate Governance analysis finds that investor expectations for board-level AI oversight now extend to whether companies have defined accountability structures, escalation triggers, measurement frameworks, and board-use rules for AI—making a named responsible committee no longer sufficient for proxy-season disclosure.

entries.title: SpaceXAI Faces Up to $6.1M in Fines for Unpermitted Mississippi Data Center Construction; Federal Court Also Voids Gas Turbine Air Permits
entries.summary: Mississippi regulators cited SpaceXAI subsidiary MZX Tech LLC for stormwater permit violations on its Southaven campus (potential $6.1M at $25K/day), while a separate federal court ruling found that 69 natural gas turbines were operated without air permits—a finding central to an ongoing NAACP lawsuit challenging the facility's environmental compliance.

entries.title: Grant Thornton Survey: Boards Flag AI Ownership Gap as Controls Remain Undocumented Ahead of Regulatory Scrutiny
entries.summary: Grant Thornton's survey of executives and board members found AI governance among the top sources of anticipated regulatory scrutiny, with board participants identifying unclear AI ownership and decision rights as central problems, and advising organizations to document governance processes, maintain AI audit trails, and preserve evidence that controls are operating.

entries.title: HaluCheck: 42k-Instance Benchmark Finds LLMs Struggle to Detect Hallucinations in Agent Trajectories Beyond Sample-Level Detection
entries.summary: arXiv:2611.08231 introduces HaluCheck, a 42,000-instance bilingual benchmark covering both factual text hallucinations and faithfulness hallucinations in agent trajectories; experiments across 14 LLMs find that models show basic sample-level detection ability but struggle with fine-grained localization, correction, and agent trajectory hallucination detection—with thinking, web search, and SFT each providing only partial improvements.

entries.title: Forrester: AI Coding Agents Expand the Security Boundary Beyond What Traditional Tools Can Assess
entries.summary: A Forrester analyst commentary argues that AI coding agents introduce a security perimeter—covering AI models, MCP servers, skills, hooks, extensions, and plugins—that existing traditional security tooling cannot evaluate, and advises compliance teams to maintain dependency inventories, require workflow-specific vendor testing, validate AI-generated code, and strengthen access and monitoring controls.
